c.tagline: Gateway to the Arctic - northern lights, midnight sun, and the world's northernmost everything.

taxi.fareNote: There is no Uber or Bolt in Tromso - taxis are the only on-demand option and are expensive. Fares are metered with high base rates plus night and weekend surcharges; book by phone or app (Din Taxi Tromso / 07902) or use a rank rather than hailing. Airport runs cost roughly 150-250 NOK.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police, 113 is the ambulance service and 110 is fire; 112 also works as the general European emergency number.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The compact historic heart on the eastern shore of Tromsoya island, lined with colorful wooden houses, the Storgata shopping street, the wooden Tromso Cathedral and the harbor; it packs in the restaurants, bars, museums and tour operators, and is where nearly every visitor stays.

The mainland district just across the bridge, home to the soaring Arctic Cathedral (Ishavskatedralen) and the Fjellheisen cable car up Storsteinen for the classic city-and-fjord panorama; mostly residential with big views.

A calm waterfront residential area on the southern tip of Tromsoya, next to the Telegrafbukta park and beach and the Polar Museum's outdoor trails; good for a quiet stay within a short walk or bus ride of the centre.

The northeastern district built around the University of Tromso, the University Hospital and the coastal-ferry quay; practical and affordable, with student cafes and easy bus links, if a little removed from the old centre.

A quieter suburban gateway across the bridge on Kvaloya (Whale Island), with fjord views and quick access to hiking, dog-sledding and northern-lights country; suits travelers with a car who want nature at the doorstep.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe everywhere in Norway.

transit.hours: Buses run from roughly 6:00 AM to around 11:00 PM-midnight, with reduced weekend and evening frequency and dedicated night buses (nattbuss) on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: Buy tickets in the Svipper app or tap a contactless bank card on board; single adult tickets are about 39 NOK (roughly $3.70) and a 24-hour ticket about 100 NOK. There is no metro, tram or local rail - Tromso is served entirely by city and regional buses run by Troms fylkestrafikk.

bus: Regional coaches to Narvik, Alta and Finnmark
ferry: Local car and passenger ferries to nearby islands

transit.m: Flybussen airport coach to the city centre and hotels (~10-15 min)
City bus 40 or 42 to the centre (~15-20 min)
Taxi to city centre (~10 min); no Uber or Bolt in Tromso

tip.r: Service is included; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but never expected.
